Variational inequalities · SETTING 291

Higher-order strongly monotone variational inequalities on compact convex sets with tangent residual

CV_S_STRONG_HIGH_VI_TANGENT

Certified restart of a monotone full-jet solver and strong-monotonicity calibration of a random-frame family give scoped bounds for constrained tangent residuals. Constants depend on the fixed derivative order.

01

Setting specification

Task

Solve $0\in F(x)+N_X(x)$ on a known compact convex set, measured by the original-domain tangent residual.

Admissible model

Fix an integer $p\ge2$. Public inputs are $d\ge1$, a nonempty compact convex $X\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ with $\operatorname{diam}(X)\le D$, a feasible $x_0$, and $L_p,\mu,D,\varepsilon>0$.

The hidden operator is $C^{p-1}$ on an open neighborhood of $X$. On $X$, $\langle F(x)-F(y),x-y\rangle\ge\mu\|x-y\|_2^2$ and $\|D^{p-1}F(x)-D^{p-1}F(y)\|_{\rm op}\le L_p\|x-y\|_2$. The declared moduli are promises: actual strong monotonicity may exceed $\mu$ and actual derivative Lipschitz modulus may be smaller than $L_p$.

No bounds on lower derivatives, $\|F\|$, or a scalar potential are imposed. Compactness and continuity give a VI solution; strong monotonicity makes it unique. The solution can be a boundary point with nonzero $F$.

Oracle interface

At any feasible $x\in X$, receive the exact complete operator jet $(F(x),DF(x),\ldots,D^{p-1}F(x))$. No values outside $X$ and no free resolvent of the unknown operator are available.

Projection onto the known $X$ and exact solves of models formed only from public geometry and returned Taylor coefficients are free internal operations. Adding a known affine regularization to a returned jet requires no extra information.

Output

Return a feasible point $\widehat x\in X$, possibly unqueried. The upper witness additionally returns $n\in N_X(\widehat x)$ and an evaluated $F(\widehat x)$; this stronger certificate is not required of lower-bound algorithms.

Loss or accuracy criterion

$r_{\rm tan}(x)=\operatorname{dist}(0,F(x)+N_X(x))$, with $N_X(x)=\{n:\langle n,z-x\rangle\le0\ \forall z\in X\}$. This is neither the weak Minty gap nor distance to the solution.

Resource accounting

Count one unit for each complete jet query, including nested subproblem work, repeated points, restarts and the final certificate evaluation. The budget is a fixed cap on every execution, not expected work. The main minimax quantity takes the worst case over all finite dimensions and legal public sets and starts; dimension is supplied to the algorithm.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Arbitrary measurable adaptive policies and outputs are allowed, with an independent private random seed and no span, zero-respecting or tensor-update restriction. All queried points must be feasible. Exact arithmetic and storage are uncharged.

For every fixed admissible instance, $\Pr(r_{\rm tan}(\widehat x)\le\varepsilon)\ge2/3$. Only the algorithm seed is random. The deterministic upper witness succeeds on every instance.

B1

Certified restart on the original compact domain

Optimal High-Order Methods for Solving Monotone Variational Inequalities ↗Local argument in this profile · see complete PDF / LaTeX ↗
Conditions
$p\ge2$ fixed and $L_p,\mu,D,\varepsilon>0$; either $\kappa_D<\kappa_{0,p}$ or $\theta>1/16$.; All eight-axis contracts of this profile hold. The upper witness is deterministic; the lower class is unrestricted randomized with fixed success probability 2/3 and fixed pathwise query cap.
Dimension conditions
Every finite dimension.
Algorithm scope
Deterministic feasible algorithms returning an evaluated tangent certificate.
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Oracle correspondence
Only feasible complete operator jets are queried; all nested calls and final evaluations are charged.
Output rule
The target is the tangent residual for the original X. The upper witness returns an actual original-domain normal certificate; the lower bound permits arbitrary feasible outputs.
Constants
Constants depend only on the fixed integer p and the once-fixed smooth gate. The threshold and sufficient dimension are explicit; no uniform claim as p grows is made.
Derivation
Theorem 5.1 of 2609.23557v1, with Assumptions 2.1--2.4, Algorithm 1 and Lemma 2.1, returns a feasible $u$ and an evaluated vector $v=F(u)+n$, $n\in N_X(u)$, with $\|v\|\le\eta$ in at most $C_p[1+(L_pR^p/\eta)^{\alpha_p}]$ complete-jet calls whenever $\|z-x^\star\|\le R$, where $\alpha_p=2/(3p-1)$. The constant $C_p$ depends only on fixed $p$. The source writes its scale as the exact initial distance. A supplied upper bound $R$ is sufficient: choose its equation (8) with $\eta_0=(L_pR^{p-1})^{-1}$ and its inner tolerance with $R$. In the proof of Theorem 4.1, equations (11)--(13) use the initial distance only through the upper estimates $\|z-x^\star\|\le R$, $\sum_t\|e_t\|\le R$, $\|u_t-x^\star\|\le2R$ and $P_0\le6R^2/\eta_0$. The distance-energy and query-sum bounds in Lemma 5.1 and Theorem 5.1 then keep the same scale. Thus the subroutine requires no knowledge of the exact distance. For the unique VI solution choose $n^\star=-F(x^\star)\in N_X(x^\star)$. Monotonicity of the normal cone and $\mu$-strong monotonicity give $\mu\|u-x^\star\|^2\le\langle F(u)+n,u-x^\star\rangle\le\|v\|\|u-x^\star\|$, hence $\|u-x^\star\|\le\|v\|/\mu$. Set $R_j=D2^{-j}$, $z_0=x_0$, and $S=\max\{1,\lceil\log_2(\mu D/\varepsilon)\rceil\}$. At each $j=0,\ldots,S-1$, run the certified monotone solver on the same original set $X$, starting from $z_j$, with residual tolerance $\eta_j=\mu R_j/2$. Set $z_{j+1}=u_j$. The preceding inequality inductively proves $\|z_{j+1}-x^\star\|\le R_{j+1}$. The last actual certificate obeys $\|v_{S-1}\|\le\mu D2^{-S}\le\varepsilon$. The final conclusion is therefore a tangent-residual certificate, not merely distance contraction. The normal cone remains $N_X$ throughout: there is no restriction to an intersected ball and no normal-cone transfer. Every stage costs at most $C_p[1+2^{\alpha_p}\kappa_D^{\alpha_p}2^{-j\alpha_p(p-1)}]$, where $\kappa_D=L_pD^{p-1}/\mu$. Summing gives $C_p[S+2^{\alpha_p}\kappa_D^{\alpha_p}/(1-2^{-\alpha_p(p-1)})]$. For fixed $p\ge2$ this is $O_p(1+\kappa_D^{\alpha_p}+\log_+(1/\theta))$, where $\theta=\varepsilon/(\mu D)$ and $\log_+(t)=\max\{0,\log t\}$. The cost includes all inner jet evaluations and all returned certificates. All queried centers and model solutions in source Algorithms 1--3 are in $X$, with projection onto the known $X$. A regularized operator $F+\eta^{-1}(\cdot-z)$ uses one original jet per query and has the same Lipschitz bound on $D^{p-1}$ for $p\ge2$. Source Assumptions 2.3--2.4 impose their inequalities on $X$; the neighborhood regularity used here supplies the same Taylor data. The bound is dimension-independent; constants are not asserted uniform when $p$ grows.
Gap or comparison
No parameter-dependent lower bound is recorded outside the calibrated chain window; the upper bound remains valid.

The lower bound holds on $X=B_2^d(D/2)$ with start zero whenever $d\ge m+\lceil2048m^3\log(8(m^2+1))\rceil$. Here $B_p=\max\{1,\|\rho^{(p-1)}\|_\infty\}$ for the fixed gate of 2609.13462v2, $c_p^{\rm sc}=1/(2^pB_p16^{p-1})$, and $\kappa_{0,p}=2^{(3p-1)/2}/c_p^{\rm sc}$. Upper bounds hold in every finite dimension. The comparison quantity takes a worst case over finite dimensions.

Conditions
$p\ge2$ fixed, $\kappa_D\ge\kappa_{0,p}$, $0<\theta\le1/16$, and $\log_+(1/\theta)\le\kappa_D^{\alpha_p}$.; All eight-axis contracts of this profile hold. The upper witness is deterministic; the lower class is unrestricted randomized with fixed success probability 2/3 and fixed pathwise query cap.; The stronger explicit statement is $T^\star_{{\rm rand},\infty}\ge m\ge\frac12(c_p^{\rm sc}\kappa_D)^{\alpha_p}$.
Dimension conditions
For fixed $p$, take $m=\lfloor(c_p^{\rm sc}\kappa_D)^{\alpha_p}\rfloor\ge2$. The lower bound holds on $X=B_2^d(D/2)$ with start zero whenever $d\ge m+\lceil2048m^3\log(8(m^2+1))\rceil$. Here $B_p=\max\{1,\|\rho^{(p-1)}\|_\infty\}$ for the fixed gate of 2609.13462v2, $c_p^{\rm sc}=1/(2^pB_p16^{p-1})$, and $\kappa_{0,p}=2^{(3p-1)/2}/c_p^{\rm sc}$. Upper bounds hold in every finite dimension. The comparison quantity takes a worst case over finite dimensions.
Algorithm scope
Arbitrary randomized adaptive feasible full-jet queries and outputs.
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Oracle correspondence
Only feasible complete operator jets are queried; all nested calls and final evaluations are charged.
Output rule
The target is the tangent residual for the original X. The upper witness returns an actual original-domain normal certificate; the lower bound permits arbitrary feasible outputs.
Constants
Constants depend only on the fixed integer p and the once-fixed smooth gate. The threshold and sufficient dimension are explicit; no uniform claim as p grows is made.
Derivation
Use only the family in 2609.13462v2, Section 10. Fix its smooth even gate $\rho$ and $B_p=\max\{1,\|\rho^{(p-1)}\|_\infty\}$. For integer $m\ge2$, set $R=D/2$, $q=1-1/(2m)$, $c=R/(2\sqrt m)$, $\tau=R/(16m^{3/2})$ and $\lambda=L_p\tau^{p-1}/B_p$, exactly as equation (10.4). For a hidden orthonormal frame $V=(v_1,\ldots,v_m)$ define $T_V(x)=cv_1+q\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}h_\tau(\langle v_i,x\rangle)v_{i+1}$ and $F_V=\lambda(\operatorname{Id}-T_V)$ on the public ball $X=B_2^d(R)$, with public start $0$. Lemma 10.2 gives global strong monotonicity $\mu_m=\lambda/(2m)$, Lipschitz $(p-1)$st derivative at most $L_p$, a unique interior zero and $r_{\rm tan}(x)=\|F_V(x)\|$ even at the boundary. No change of target metric is required. Writing $a_p=(3p-1)/2$ and $c_p^{\rm sc}=1/(2^pB_p16^{p-1})$, direct substitution gives $\mu_m=c_p^{\rm sc}L_pD^{p-1}/m^{a_p}$. The residual barrier in equation (11.3) is $L_pR^p/[8B_p16^{p-1}m^{a_p}]=\mu_mD/8$. Assume $\kappa_D\ge\kappa_{0,p}:=2^{a_p}/c_p^{\rm sc}$ and set $m=\lfloor(c_p^{\rm sc}\kappa_D)^{1/a_p}\rfloor\ge2$. Then $m^{a_p}\le c_p^{\rm sc}\kappa_D$, so $\mu_m\ge\mu$. The hard family is therefore inside the promised $\mu$-strongly monotone class; the modulus is an available lower bound, not an equality requirement. Apply Theorem 11.3 with the fixed cap $N=m-1$ and source failure parameter $\delta=1/4$. It requires $d\ge m+\lceil2048m^3\log(8(m^2+1))\rceil$. For every adaptive randomized algorithm with this cap and any feasible measurable output, some fixed frame has probability at least $3/4$ of residual at least $\mu_mD/8$. If $0<\theta\le1/16$, this barrier is at least $\mu D/8\ge2\varepsilon$. A per-instance success guarantee of $2/3$ is therefore impossible with $m-1$ queries. Consequently $T^\star_{{\rm rand},\infty}\ge m\ge\frac12(c_p^{\rm sc}\kappa_D)^{\alpha_p}=\Omega_p(\kappa_D^{\alpha_p})$. The same fixed-dimensional statement holds for every $d$ satisfying the displayed sufficient threshold, on the public ball family. The source discloses all scalar parameters and even the template, while only the frame is hidden. Declaring $\mu$ and calibrating $m$ from public parameters does not invalidate its information argument. The bound is for arbitrary randomized complete-jet queries, not a span-restricted algorithm class. For fixed $p$, the sufficient dimension is $O_p(\kappa_D^{6/(3p-1)}\log(2+\kappa_D))$; the explicit threshold above is authoritative. No lower bound of this order is asserted in every fixed small dimension, or for the additive accuracy logarithm.
Upper bound
\[O_p\!\left(1+\kappa_D^{\alpha_p}+\log_+(1/\theta)\right)\]

Theorem 5.1 of 2609.23557v1, with Assumptions 2.1--2.4, Algorithm 1 and Lemma 2.1, returns a feasible $u$ and an evaluated vector $v=F(u)+n$, $n\in N_X(u)$, with $\|v\|\le\eta$ in at most $C_p[1+(L_pR^p/\eta)^{\alpha_p}]$ complete-jet calls whenever $\|z-x^\star\|\le R$, where $\alpha_p=2/(3p-1)$. The constant $C_p$ depends only on fixed $p$. The source writes its scale as the exact initial distance. A supplied upper bound $R$ is sufficient: choose its equation (8) with $\eta_0=(L_pR^{p-1})^{-1}$ and its inner tolerance with $R$. In the proof of Theorem 4.1, equations (11)--(13) use the initial distance only through the upper estimates $\|z-x^\star\|\le R$, $\sum_t\|e_t\|\le R$, $\|u_t-x^\star\|\le2R$ and $P_0\le6R^2/\eta_0$. The distance-energy and query-sum bounds in Lemma 5.1 and Theorem 5.1 then keep the same scale. Thus the subroutine requires no knowledge of the exact distance. For the unique VI solution choose $n^\star=-F(x^\star)\in N_X(x^\star)$. Monotonicity of the normal cone and $\mu$-strong monotonicity give $\mu\|u-x^\star\|^2\le\langle F(u)+n,u-x^\star\rangle\le\|v\|\|u-x^\star\|$, hence $\|u-x^\star\|\le\|v\|/\mu$. Set $R_j=D2^{-j}$, $z_0=x_0$, and $S=\max\{1,\lceil\log_2(\mu D/\varepsilon)\rceil\}$. At each $j=0,\ldots,S-1$, run the certified monotone solver on the same original set $X$, starting from $z_j$, with residual tolerance $\eta_j=\mu R_j/2$. Set $z_{j+1}=u_j$. The preceding inequality inductively proves $\|z_{j+1}-x^\star\|\le R_{j+1}$. The last actual certificate obeys $\|v_{S-1}\|\le\mu D2^{-S}\le\varepsilon$. The final conclusion is therefore a tangent-residual certificate, not merely distance contraction. The normal cone remains $N_X$ throughout: there is no restriction to an intersected ball and no normal-cone transfer. Every stage costs at most $C_p[1+2^{\alpha_p}\kappa_D^{\alpha_p}2^{-j\alpha_p(p-1)}]$, where $\kappa_D=L_pD^{p-1}/\mu$. Summing gives $C_p[S+2^{\alpha_p}\kappa_D^{\alpha_p}/(1-2^{-\alpha_p(p-1)})]$. For fixed $p\ge2$ this is $O_p(1+\kappa_D^{\alpha_p}+\log_+(1/\theta))$, where $\theta=\varepsilon/(\mu D)$ and $\log_+(t)=\max\{0,\log t\}$. The cost includes all inner jet evaluations and all returned certificates. All queried centers and model solutions in source Algorithms 1--3 are in $X$, with projection onto the known $X$. A regularized operator $F+\eta^{-1}(\cdot-z)$ uses one original jet per query and has the same Lipschitz bound on $D^{p-1}$ for $p\ge2$. Source Assumptions 2.3--2.4 impose their inequalities on $X$; the neighborhood regularity used here supplies the same Taylor data. The bound is dimension-independent; constants are not asserted uniform when $p$ grows.
Gap or comparison
$O_p(1+\log_+(1/\theta)/\kappa_D^{\alpha_p})$. No matching lower bound for the additive accuracy logarithm is asserted.
